findings.explanation: root_block_device.volume_type is hardcoded to "standard", AWS's oldest magnetic EBS type. It has the worst latency/IOPS-per-dollar of any EBS type and is not billed or provisioned like SSD-backed volumes (gp3/gp2). For a database node where disk I/O directly drives read/write/compaction latency, this both costs more for a given performance target and delivers materially worse performance than gp3 at the same size. AWS also discourages new use of 'standard' volumes.
findings.remediation: Change volume_type to "gp3" (optionally exposing iops/throughput as variables). Note: verify in a plan first — some provider versions treat root_block_device.volume_type changes as requiring resource replacement, which matters for a stateful Cassandra node even though delete_on_termination=false protects the underlying volume.
findings.title: Cassandra data node root volume uses legacy 'standard' (magnetic) EBS type

findings.explanation: The user_data template computes seeds = "${var.private_ips[0]},${var.private_ips[2]}" for every instance, independent of count.index. This expression evaluates for all count instances regardless of cluster size: if var.private_ips has fewer than 3 elements (a 1- or 2-node cluster, which the module otherwise permits since count = length(var.private_ips) has no lower bound), the [2] index is out of range and every instance in the plan fails. Even on valid 3+ node clusters, skipping index 1 for the seed list is an arbitrary, undocumented choice with no comment explaining why index 1 is excluded.
findings.remediation: Compute seeds from a bounded slice instead of fixed literal indices, e.g. join(",", slice(var.private_ips, 0, min(3, length(var.private_ips)))), and/or add a variable validation on private_ips requiring length >= 3 if smaller clusters are genuinely unsupported.
findings.title: Cassandra seed list hardcodes indices [0] and [2], breaking on clusters smaller than 3 nodes

findings.explanation: Neither resource sets a tags block, and the module exposes no tags/tags_default variable. Consumers can't attach cost-allocation, ownership, or environment tags to the instances or security group this module creates, which hampers cost tracking and resource identification across the 3 example roots that all invoke this module.
findings.note: Initially fixed via a module-level tags variable, then deliberately reverted: tagging is handled by provider-level default_tags in each consuming root instead, which merges onto every resource automatically without the module needing its own tags plumbing.
findings.remediation: Add a `variable "tags"` (type = map(string), default = {}) and set `tags = var.tags` on both aws_instance.cassandra and aws_security_group.cassandra.
findings.title: aws_instance.cassandra and aws_security_group.cassandra have no tags

findings.explanation: Storage sizing for a database node is an environment-specific decision (dev vs. prod data volumes differ significantly), but volume_size = 100 is a fixed literal with no variable, forcing anyone needing a different size to fork the module.
findings.remediation: Add a `variable "volume_size"` (type = number, default = 100) and reference it in root_block_device.
findings.title: root_block_device.volume_size is hardcoded to 100 GB

suggested_policies.rationale: EBS 'standard' (magnetic) volumes are AWS's legacy, highest-latency, worst-cost-per-IOPS volume type. Any root_block_device or aws_ebs_volume pinned to volume_type = "standard" is almost always an oversight rather than an intentional choice, and is deterministically detectable.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_AWS_XXX
name: EBS volumes should not use the legacy 'standard' (magnetic) volume type
principle: cost
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  The 'standard' EBS volume type is magnetic storage with the worst
  latency and IOPS-per-dollar of any EBS type. gp3 offers better
  performance at lower cost for nearly all workloads.
remediation: |
  Use gp3 (or io2 for high-IOPS needs) instead:
    root_block_device {
      volume_type = "gp3"
    }
resources:
  aws_instance:
    path: root_block_device.volume_type
    not_equals: "standard"
